title: Real business cycles
about: The RBC model with a choice of hours: one technology shock, eight variables. A good place to start.

title: Stochastic growth model
about: The smallest model with a decision in it: consumption against saving, five variables, a steady state in closed form.
source: Written for the workbench; the model of dsge.rbc() in Cozy.

title: New Keynesian, three equations
about: Phillips curve, IS curve and a policy rule. Lower phi_pi below one and the equilibrium is no longer unique.
source: Written for the workbench, after Gali (2015), ch. 3.

title: Collard's RBC (Dynare example1)
about: A growth model with two correlated shocks, technology and preferences.

title: Schorfheide (2000), cash in advance
about: A monetary model with money growth and technology shocks, leads of two periods and a closed-form steady state.
source: Dynare 6.0, examples/fs2000.mod, unmodified; its estimation commands are passed over.

title: Gali (2015), baseline New Keynesian
about: The textbook model in full: fourteen variables, three shocks, and a price level with a unit root.
source: Model block from Dynare 6.0, examples/Gali_2015.mod (Johannes Pfeifer); estimation part removed, shocks set.

title: Fernandez-Villaverde (2010), baseline New Keynesian
about: A medium-scale model in nonlinear form: 28 variables, five shocks, sticky prices and wages, habits, adjustment costs and trend growth.
source: Model block from Dynare 6.0, examples/NK_baseline.mod (Benjamin Born and Johannes Pfeifer); its separate steady-state file written into the model file.

title: Smets and Wouters (2007)
about: The medium-scale model of the US economy: forty variables, seven shocks, sticky prices and wages, at the posterior mode.
source: Johannes Pfeifer's DSGE_mod collection, Smets_Wouters_2007_45.mod, unmodified; its estimation commands are passed over.
